newsitem.title: USA: Gateway to launch big screen PC/TV with DVD.
newsitem.headline: Gateway to launch big screen PC/TV with DVD.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc said it will launch on Thursday its Destination Big Screen PC/TV including new digital versatile disk (DVD) technology.

Gateway, a direct marketer of personal computers and related equipment, said the new system is part of its strategy to lead in the "convergence market", combining computers and other devices such as televisions.

DVD disks look like compact disks (CDs) used for music and computer applications, but hold more and have higher image quality. A DVD disk, for example, will hold up to 133 minutes of video or 4.7 Gigabytes of data, comparable to seven CDs, and that will expand as the technology is improved, Gateway said.
The DVD-equipped big screen PC/TVs start at $3,199 each, said Stacy Hand, Gateway's Destination product marketing manager.

"DVD at this point in time is an emerging market, so we don't expect revenues to be extremely huge," Hand said, adding, however, the company expects the technology to be more widespread by the Christmas gift-buying season.
"It's hard to put a dollar amount on it," Hand said of the revenue potential from the new product. "It's more of keeping the competitive advantage over our competition."
DVD quality is also better than CDs, laser disks and videos, Gateway said. The company said it expects its new PC/TV to be used for both educational and entertaiment applications.
"Imagine playing Doom on a 31-inch monitor with surround sound," Hand said, referring to a popular computer game.
"There is no question DVD is going to take off, it's a question of when," he added.
